correctness.rationale: For every odd prime \(q\ge5\) and \(1\le p<q\), the equality \(F^q(z)=z\) implies that the integer itinerary-sign polynomial vanishes at a primitive \(q\)-th root. Its degree at most \(q-1\) forces a multiple of \(\Phi_q\), so all signs coincide. The constant-sign affine rotation has center \(\pm\lambda/(\lambda-1)\) and exactly \(q\) evenly spaced half-plane constraints. Averaging gives the empty orientation phase; in the nonempty phase they yield a closed and an open regular \(q\)-gon, both of inradius \(-\cot(\pi p/q)/2\). The regions are exhaustive, all noncenter points have least period \(q\), and the polygon area law is uniquely maximized at \(p=q-1\). The companion program passed 4236 finite checks but does not replace the all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The first public source arXiv:2306.17543 (Theorems A, B and section 4) provides regular-tile periodicity, a polygon-side bound, and a concrete pentagon for \(8\pi/5\), but no complete \(\operatorname{Fix}(F^q)\) census for all odd primes, mixed-sign exclusion, or total area and optimizer. The broader Goetz–Quas 2009 Lemma 11 concerns centers visiting both half-planes, so its two-sided height hypotheses do not hold for the constant-sign fixed-center resonance polygons. The 2020/2022 Cima et al. paper treats selected small denominators, including \(q=3\), which is excluded by \(q\ge5\). Actual targeted searches found no theorem implying the whole claim. This is best-knowledge priority, with risk of unindexed earlier equivalents.
residual_risks: An unindexed or difficult-to-retrieve published formulation may already give the complete one-branch q-resonance census or its area as a consequence; the search cannot establish absolute priority.
The area formula is elementary once one has the prime-q global itinerary exclusion and polygons; its value is in the complete dynamical classification, not a claim of a difficult integration.
The lower-branch open boundary depends on the convention H(z)=1 on Im(z)=0; the total measure does not.

value.rationale: The mass of the period-dividing-\(q\) locus and its presence/absence are canonical dynamical invariants. Prime cyclotomic rigidity proves a global no-mixed-itinerary theorem, giving an exhaustive answer rather than a constructed example. For every odd prime \(q\ge5\), orientation decides whether the first-resonance locus vanishes; an exact polygon area formula distinguishes all numerators in the nonempty phase, has a unique maximizing numerator, and produces \(q^2/(2\pi)\) growth as the rotation approaches identity. This is a motivated short-period classification rather than a mere rewriting of known tile existence. The restricted scope and simple area computation are openly stated.
